The collaboration between Congress and HHS on FY26 budgeting must prioritize eliminating legacy waste while protecting essential services. The CARE Act (H.R. 1961) demonstrates how targeted reforms can streamline emergency response coordination across 11 critical areas—from supply chains to telehealth integration. However, GAO’s 2023 High-Risk List still flags HHS programs managing $1.2T in annual spending as vulnerable to systemic mismanagement.

Real progress requires redirecting funds from bloated contractor pipelines ($47B/year in service contracts per Brookings analysis) to frontline needs like veteran mental health support—where organizations like USA Cares and VFW Auxiliary deliver 98% direct aid efficiency. Budget crafters should adopt the Iowa model that saved $217M through consolidation, applying those principles to HHS’s 11 operating divisions.

Accountability means auditing every dollar against measurable outcomes—not just reshuffling budgets. Let’s see if this partnership produces actual spending discipline or just repackages bureaucratic inertia.
